conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you. We’ll use a brief, well-studied form called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s 10 questions about the past week, and it helps us spot moms who might be struggling with postpartum depression or anxiety. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the small team who looks after your care. We’ll go one question at a time, and you can answer however feels most comfortable. Ready to start?

First question: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi Sarah… I guess I’m ready.

Um… laughing? Not really. I mean, if my husband shows me a cute meme I might give a little smile, but it doesn’t come easily. Most of the time I’m just tired or worried about the baby, so finding things genuinely funny feels kind of out of reach right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… not really. I can force a little chuckle if someone cracks a joke, but it doesn’t feel natural or lift my mood the way it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much, honestly. Even little things I used to get excited about—like my favorite show or a walk with a friend—feel more like chores right now. I still *want* to enjoy them, but the spark just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like last night when the baby wouldn’t settle—my brain kept whispering it was because I’m not doing something right, even though my partner says it’s normal. It’s not constant, but those “it’s my fault” thoughts pop up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… a few times this week I’ve caught myself just sitting there with my heart racing, worrying that the baby’s breathing is off or that I’ll miss some cue and something bad will happen. Nothing’s actually wrong, but the worry sort of barges in anyway.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of nights I’ve woken up suddenly with this tight chest and racing heart, sure something awful was about to happen—then I peek in the bassinet, everything’s fine, but it still takes a while to shake the shaky feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days I feel like I’m barely treading water. The baby naps for twenty minutes and I’m rushing to finish bottles, laundry, maybe grab a bite, and then he’s up again. It’s not that I can’t do it, just that by evening I’m exhausted and teary, thinking “how can I keep this up tomorrow?”
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly “unhappy,” more… keyed-up and overwhelmed. Once I finally lie down, my mind keeps replaying every little cry or feed, worrying I’ll sleep through something. I drop off eventually, but it takes a while, and I wake up a couple of times feeling on-edge even when the baby’s still asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve had moments—usually late afternoon—where this heavy sadness just settles in. Yesterday I looked at the baby sleeping and instead of feeling warm I felt this wave of “I’m not doing enough,” and my eyes welled up. It’s not all day, but those pockets of gloom hit a few times this week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really, no. I’ve gotten teary a couple of times, but actual crying—like sobbing—hasn’t happened. It feels more like a lump in my throat that I push down so I can keep going.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’m tired and overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, self-report via EPDS-style questionnaire  
Date: [today]  
SCREENER: [your name], Licensed Mental Health Counselor  

A. Endorsed Symptoms (≥ moderate frequency/intensity)  
- Anhedonia / low pleasure (Q1, Q2)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt (Q3)  
- Free-floating anxiety & nocturnal panic episodes (Q4, Q5)  
- Feeling overwhelmed, “treading water,” daily tearfulness (Q6, Q8)  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia linked to racing thoughts about infant safety (Q7)  

B. Pattern  
Persistent low mood with prominent anxiety symptoms beginning shortly after delivery; no suicidal ideation reported (Q10 denied).  

C. Screening Significance  
Scores suggest elevated risk for:  
1. Major depressive episode with peripartum onset  
2. Generalized anxiety / panic spectrum symptoms comorbid with postpartum status  

D. Risk Factors Identified  
- Loss of pleasure + daily sadness  
- Insomnia secondary to mood rather than infant demands alone  
- Recurrent guilt cognitions  
- Physiological arousal / panic without medical cause  
- Self-harm ideation: NEGATIVE (no further safety action indicated at present)  

E. Clinical Observation  
Findings exceed “baby blues” threshold; further evaluation (structured diagnostic interview, PHQ-9, GAD-7, psychosocial stressors, supports, medical rule-out) recommended to determine need for treatment or referral.
